newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Saflife details JCI funding plans.
newsitem.headline: Saflife details JCI funding plans.

text.p: Financial services group Saflife Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to raise 2.25 billion rand via a rights offer and 154.6 million by way of an offer of warrants to finance the African Mining Group's (AMG) purchase of a controlling stake in mining house JCI Ltd.
At the same time, the parties involved in the JCI deal -- which will see the mining house transferred into black hands -- said that the acquisition terms had been restructured.

Saflife will pay 2.47 billion rand or 54.50 rand a share for a 30 percent stake in JCI, which is being sold by Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and De Beers Consoldiated Mines Ltd. Payment will be made on May 26.
Certain members of the AMG consortium have been granted an option over a further 4.9 percent of JCI for one year at 54.50 a share.
The restructuring means the acquisition of the JCI stake will be completed at a reduced level of 30 percent with certain AMG members given extra time to participate in the transaction.

Saflife said it would be issuing 112.5 million new shares at 20 rand on the basis of 272.9 for every held. A total of 41.2 million warrants will be issued at 3.75 rand on basis of 100 for every 100 shares held. The warrants are convertible into 41.2 million new shares at 20 rand each.
Last date to register for the share offer is April 25 and May 23 for the warrant offer.
The rights offer and JCI funding deal will transform Saflife, which is controlled by Mzi Khumalo, AMG and Hosken Consolidated Investments Ltd, into a major mining force.
As a result, the directors will seek to transfer the listing of Saflife from the Insurance to the Financial Mining Houses sector of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
In a separate announcement, Investec Investment Trust Ltd said it planned to raise 200 million rand to follow its rights in Saflife.
